newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to cut wheat import tax.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to cut wheat import tax.

text.p: Turkey is planning to reduce a 15-percent tax on wheat imports in a bid to cut the cost of imports, a grain official said on Thursday.
The official said the state grain agency (TMO) planned to import up to 500,000 tonnes.
"The 15-percent customs tax on wheat imports will be reduced," said the official, who declined to be named.

He would not say what the new tax level would be, but traders and grain sources said it could be either three percent, which it had been until it was raised to 15 percent in September 21, or even zero percent.
"The TMO has been authorised to import up to 500,000 tonnes but this does not necessarily mean the import level would be that much," he said.

Turkey has been considering wheat imports since last week to stop a rise in bread prices which have gone up about 30 percent in the past three weeks following a clampdown on wheat imports from the United States over concerns that they might contain ergot fungus.
The government later said it would ease a zero-tolerance level for ergot fungus, which is practically impossible to achieve, to 0.05 percent.
But this move was not seen as satisfactory by the United States government, which is still not issuing health certificates for grain exports to Turkey.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told reporters on Thursday the government's pledge to bring down the price of bread to 15,000 lira per loaf on a nationwise basis from the current 18,000 lira would be fulfilled.
"From Friday (November 15) bread prices will be 15,000 lira," he said before a cabinet meeting. He did not give other details.
The TMO will also be authorised to sell wheat from its stocks of about 700,000 tonnes of milling wheat to curb bread price rises.
Turkey raised customs taxes on imports of wheat, non-seed corn, sunflower seed oil in September, saying the harvest of these crops would be good in 1996/97.
